author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The three late theological novels—VALIS (1981), The Divine Invasion (1981), and The Transmigration of Timothy Archer (1982)—in which Dick works his 1974 visionary experience into fiction, asking across all three whether authentic divine contact is possible in a world that may be false.
page_summary:
VALIS splits Dick into the skeptical narrator 'Phil' and his mad alter ego Horselover Fat, who believes a beam of pink light has transmitted divine knowledge to him from an intelligence called VALIS (Vast Active Living Intelligence System); the two chase a film that seems to encode the same contact, staging Dick's crisis as a study in whether revelation can be told apart from psychosis. The Divine Invasion turns to incarnation: a child born of an alien union is God returning to a corrupted world hostile to divinity, and the novel plays as theology in the register of tragedy. The Transmigration of Timothy Archer, Dick's last and most naturalistic novel, follows a bishop who dies seeking the historical roots of Christ, narrated by the woman who survives him, and asks how one recognizes an authentic Christ figure in a world crowded with false ones.

Across the three, the shared project is a lived, unsettled theology drawn from gnosticism: the world is a false creation, the true God is hidden or imprisoned, and caritas—involuntary, self-sacrificing love—is the sole reliable mark of authentic divinity. Dick refuses to resolve whether VALIS is God, extraterrestrial, or delusion, dramatizing instead the agony of not knowing. The novels are the fictional face of the vast Exegesis he was writing at the same time to interpret his own experience.

Though written and set as a loose trilogy of theological inquiry rather than a continuous story, the three books are Dick's culminating work. Transmigration was completed shortly before his death in 1982; the omnibus gathers them as the summa of his final, visionary period.

biography_events.event: Publishes The Divine Invasion as the second novel in the VALIS trilogy
